lots.what_it_is: Our Island Home: A Tasmanian Sketch Book by Louisa A. Meredith (J. Walch & Sons, Hobart / Marcus Ward & Co, London, 1879), cloth with gilt pine-cone and she-oak design, autotype plates.

asking.venue: Hard to Find Books NZ, Dunedin (via AbeBooks)
asking.note: ASKING, same_item yes, page opened. Same 1879 Walch/Marcus Ward edition, graded VG-: heavy scuffing to spine and board edges, foxing, gift inscription, two plates partly detached. Lot 852 is probably a bit worse (frayed spine ends, back board covered with pasted glider clippings and photos). Rate 1 USD = 1.4286 AUD (open.er-api.com, 21 Oct 2026); researcher's 1.55 was too high. Only copy on AbeBooks. Dealer asking price, not a price paid.

lots.guide_summary: Only one entry survives: one ASKING price (AbeBooks NZ dealer, about A$819 for a VG- copy). No SOLD and no UNSOLD evidence for this title. The only Gowans Meredith book sale (My Home in Tasmania, $105) is a modern dust-jacketed reprint of a different book, so it was dropped. Rate 1 USD = 1.4286 AUD.
lots.working: No SOLD entry for Our Island Home within 24 months, so no maximum bid can be set (keep 0, flip 0). The dealer ask of about A$819 is optimistic; auction hammer for a worn, defaced copy is likely well below that, but this is unproven.
lots.confidence_reason: Title and author read clearly on the cover and spine, plates captioned, but the value rests on one dealer asking price only. Web search cap was reached, so no auction records (Invaluable, Leonard Joel, Australian Book Auctions) were checked; Australian Book Auctions returned 503.
lots.condition: Cloth worn and rubbed with pale spotting, spine ends frayed, foxing and some toning to plate margins, back pastedown or board covered by pasted 1930s-style newspaper clippings and glider photographs. Completeness of plates and text unknown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Front board reads 'Our Island Home / A Tasmanian Sketch Book by Louisa A Meredith', spine 'Our Island Home'. Plates seen: Hobart Town, Mt Direction &c. from Proctor's Road; South Arm from the Springs; Herne Bay, D'Entrecasteaux's Channel; Wine-glass Bay, Schoutens; Cape Raoul, with 'Autotype' and 'London' imprints. Last photo shows clippings and glider photos pasted over the back board, which hurts collector value. Gowans title calls it 'A Tasmanian Sketchbook ... some wear'.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are all the plates present and attached (please count them), is the title page present with Walch/Marcus Ward imprint and date, are the clippings pasted only on the back pastedown or on any plates or text, and is the text block sound?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped Gowans lot 385847 'BOOK: MY HOME IN TASMANIA - LOUISA ANNE MEREDITH' ($105 hammer, listed 26 Jan 2026): API opened and its photo checked, it is a modern hardback reprint in a dust jacket of a different Meredith title, not comparable. Researcher's AbeBooks figure corrected from US$571.88 to US$573.03 as now shown and re-rated at 1.4286.

lots.guide_summary: All SOLD Gowans hammers (premium extra). Four close floor or cabinet gramophones sold for $55 to $210 hammer in Jun to Oct 2026 (median about $100); tabletop and portable machines $40 to $230 as a category guide. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence gathered (web search cap reached). AUD, no conversion.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close same-type SOLD = $55 (HMV cabinet, 436700, Sep 2026). 55 / 1.198 = 45.9, round down to $45. Flip: likely resale about $120 (middle of close Gowans results $55 to $210), less about 15% selling costs (auction commission or marketplace fees, no outbound postage as it is pickup only and bulky) = $102. 102 / 2.396 = 42.6, round down to $40. All comps are close types, not the same model, and the lot 880 model number is unread.
lots.confidence_reason: HMV maker confirmed from the Nipper lid transfer and soundbox, and four close SOLD Gowans results were opened with photos checked, but none is the same model, the model plaque is unreadable and working order is unknown.
lots.condition: Cabinet looks complete and sound with general wear and some fading to the oak top. Lid stay, crank, tone arm and soundbox present, turntable felt present. Motor and spring condition unknown.
lots.key_photo_findings: HMV Nipper transfer inside the lid; soundbox reads His Master's Voice; small brass oval model plaque on the motor board (number looks like 1?2, unreadable even enlarged); crank handle in place; a red Columbia 78 on the platter; lower doors open to two record shelves and an empty lower section (internal horn area). Two-over-two door oak floor console, no visible damage.
lots.question_for_gowans: Does the motor wind and play at steady speed (is the spring intact), what model number is on the brass plaque on the motor board, and are any records included beyond the one on the turntable?
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped Gowans lot 425454 'His Master's Voice radiogram' ($260): photo shows a 1960s-70s electric stereo radiogram, a different product. Re-filed 419965 (HMV portable) from close to category guide and 417297 (Columbia floor cabinet) from category guide to close after checking photos. Added 436700 HMV gramophone $55, missed by researcher. Note 392777 not re-read on my Columbia search page, kept as a lead only.

lots.working: Keep: lowest close SOLD = $35 (423376). 35 / 1.198 = 29.2, round down to $25. Flip: likely resale about $55 (middle of close results), less about 15% seller commission if resold at auction = $46.75. 46.75 / 2.396 = 19.5, round down to $15. Thin margin: a flip only makes sense for a woodworker's own use.
lots.confidence_reason: Many opened Gowans SOLD results with photos, four of them visually similar wide slabs, but species and dimensions are not confirmed (no measurements given, no label) and Gowans' timber titles are generic.
lots.condition: Rough sawn, unfinished, live edge with some bark and voids at lower right, a few knots and small checks, no visible figure. Looks dry and flat in the photo but not confirmed.
lots.key_photo_findings: Slab chalked '1104 23/10/26' with lot sticker; pale pinkish-tan colour consistent with myrtle; plain straight grain, knots near top and lower middle, live edge on right; neighbouring lot 1105 partly visible at left. Roughly 55 to 60 cm wide and over 2 m long judged against the roller door, not measured.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. Researcher's aggregated August and September entries were re-checked against the API and photos: most are narrow boards, so they were re-filed as category guide rather than close; July wide slabs (421745, 421746, 423375, 423376) are the closest matches.
